description:
# TSNBench: Benchmarking LLM Proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking

TSNBench is the first benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN). TSN is a suite of IEEE 802.1 standards for deterministic Ethernet communication with bounded latency. It is used in safety-critical domains such as autonomous vehicles, aviation, defense and industrial automation, where an incorrect delay bound may compromise system safety.

TSNBench tests two complementary abilities:

- **Declarative TSN knowledge:** 939 expert-validated multiple-choice questions (MCQs).
- **Quantitative reasoning:** 200 open-ended Worst-Case Delay (WCD) computation tasks, 100 for the Credit-Based Shaper (CBS, IEEE 802.1Qav) and 100 for Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (CQF, IEEE 802.1Qch). An additional 10 CBS and 10 CQF test cases use the real-world Orion network topology.

The dataset accompanies the paper *TSNBench: Benchmarking LLM Proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking*, NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track.

## Dataset contents

### 1. Multiple-choice question answers (MCQAs)
- 939 questions on TSN mechanisms and concepts, including traffic shaping and scheduling (TAS, CBS, ATS, CQF), reliability and stream management (FRER, PSFP, SRP).
- The questions were generated from 83 publicly available TSN research papers and validated by five TSN experts.
- Each question has answer options and the correct answer.

### 2. Open-ended Worst-Case Delay (WCD) tasks
Each test case (TC) describes a TSN network: the topology, a set of TSN flows (period, frame size, deadline), and the route of the flows. The task is to compute the end-to-end worst-case delay of every flow for the given mechanism and constraints.

| Task | Test cases | Topologies | Ground truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| CBS (802.1Qav) | 100 | one-switch, ring, medium mesh | Network calculus (NC) analysis |
| CQF (802.1Qch) | 100 | one-switch, ring, medium mesh | Analytical CQF delay bound |
| Orion (CBS) | 10 | real-world Orion network | Network calculus (NC) analysis |

All delays are in microseconds (µs).

### 3. Prompts
- **Closed-book (CB):** the model receives only the network description.
- **Formula-in-context (FC):** the prompt also includes the WCD formula for the mechanism.
- **Prompt-sensitivity variants:** paraphrased prompts used to test robustness.

## Intended use and limitations
- TSNBench is meant for **evaluation**. Do not use it to train or fine-tune models you plan to evaluate on it.
- The open-ended tasks cover CBS and CQF. Other mechanisms (e.g. TAS) appear only in the MCQAs.
- Ground truth is computed under the network assumptions stated in the paper (e.g. cut-through switches and fixed switching, propagation and synchronization delays). 

## Folder structure
```text
TSNBench/
├── README.md
├── LICENSE
├── DATASHEET.md
├── dataset/
│   ├── mcqa/                          # 939 MCQs (JSON)
│   └── open_ended/                    # TC1–TC100: topology, flows and routes files per test case
├── evaluation_results/
│   ├── mcqa_evaluation/output/        # per-model MCQA responses
│   └── open_end_evaluation/output/
│       ├── CBS/                       # per-model WCD predictions for CBS
│       └── CQF/                       # per-model WCD predictions for CQF
└── prompts/
    ├── mcqa/                          # MCQA prompt templates
    └── open_ended/                    # CB, FC and prompt-sensitivity prompts
```

rai:dataLimitations: This dataset is intended for research benchmarking of model performance on Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) domain knowledge and worst-case delay reasoning. Its applicability is limited to the task settings, mechanisms, network assumptions, and input formats included in the dataset. The open-ended component focuses on selected TSN mechanisms, primarily Credit-Based Shaper (CBS) and Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (CQF). It does not fully cover all TSN mechanisms, such as Time-Aware Shaper (TAS), Asynchronous Traffic Shaper (ATS), or full industrial deployment constraints. The open-ended test cases are generated from controlled software-based network instances and may not capture all real-world effects, vendor-specific behavior, hardware constraints, or operational conditions in deployed TSN systems. The dataset uses fixed assumptions for network parameters, topology descriptions, routing information, traffic-flow specifications, and worst-case delay computation. This dataset is not recommended for directly configuring, validating, certifying, or deploying safety-critical TSN networks. It should not be used as a replacement for formal timing-analysis tools, certified engineering workflows, industrial TSN configuration tools, or expert validation. Model outputs evaluated using this dataset should not be used for real-world safety-critical decisions without independent verification by qualified domain experts and validated analysis tools.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain selection bias because the multiple-choice component is derived from selected open-access TSN research papers and author-available manuscript versions. As a result, TSN topics that are more frequently discussed in the selected literature may be over-represented, while topics with limited open-access coverage, proprietary industrial relevance, or stronger representation in IEEE standards rather than research papers may be under-represented. The dataset may also contain mechanism-level bias. The open-ended reasoning component focuses primarily on Credit-Based Shaper (CBS) and Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (CQF). Other TSN mechanisms and scenarios, such as Time-Aware Shaper (TAS), Asynchronous Traffic Shaper (ATS) are not equally represented. The dataset is not expected to contain demographic bias because it does not include personal, demographic, or human-subject data.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: This dataset does not contain personal or sensitive information. It does not include gender, socio-economic status, geography, language, age, culture, experience or seniority, health or medical data, political or religious beliefs, or any other personal attributes.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset has been validated for research benchmarking of model performance on two task categories: multiple-choice TSN knowledge evaluation and open-ended worst-case delay reasoning for CBS and CQF scenarios. The dataset is validated for comparing model accuracy, consistency, calibration, and numerical error under the provided benchmark settings. It is not validated for direct TSN deployment, safety certification, industrial network configuration, vendor-specific TSN implementations, or real-time re-configuration. Performance on this dataset should not be interpreted as evidence that a model is ready to configure TSN networks without independent verification by qualified engineers and validated analysis tools.
rai:dataSocialImpact: This dataset may have positive societal effects by supporting safer and more rigorous evaluation of large language models in deterministic networking and safety-critical communication domains. It may also support progress toward more reliable AI-assisted tools for industrial automation, automotive systems, aerospace communication, and other real-time networked systems where timing guarantees are important. The main negative risk is misuse of benchmark results. A model that performs well on this dataset may still be unsafe for real-world TSN configuration, deployment, certification, or timing analysis. The dataset does not contain personal, demographic, or human-subject data, so direct fairness risks for demographic groups are not expected.
